mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer spending power, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives lower S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below baseline when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below baseline during three-month periods of INDPRO contraction exceeding 1% per month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL < 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA and RSAFS > 12-month MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above baseline when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressure and inflationary expectations, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as monetary policy tightens.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below baseline when UNRATE remains below 3.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above 5% for six consecutive months signals a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader economic activity, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above baseline during six-month periods when HOUST rises by more than 5% month-over-month.
